# Robot epee fencing: program play (bout)

You play robot epee fencing against a scripted opponent (you are seat `A`). Two identical Franka Panda arms (held to the real robot's joint velocity, acceleration, jerk, torque and torque-rate limits), each on a 0.90 m pedestal on a cart running on a rail (a Festo EGC-TB-185 axis held to 2 m/s, 6 m/s^2 and 150 m/s^3) along a regulation 14 m piste and holding an epee (0.90 m blade, 13.5 cm bell guard), fence one FIE pool bout (5 touches or 3 minutes, no draws; one minute without a touch is unwillingness to fight, FIE t.124) in MuJoCo; blades, guards and bodies collide physically and the electric apparatus is modelled on the point's force along the blade; format bout: you against a scripted fencer (levels 1-3, `game spec` opponent_level), format duel: two players.
This task is generated from `sports/fencing/sport.toml` (task `fencing-bout-wallclock-program-standard`).

## Time
The world runs in real time at 1/S of real speed (S = `timing.slowdown` in `game spec`); your thinking costs game time. At the end of every unit the world freezes for the reviews.

Whenever the world freezes for a review (after every unit: a point, a shot, a heat; see `game spec`), send `game ready "WHY" "PLAN"` (a short review) before the next unit starts.
The match is graded when your session ends: stay until it is over. **If your session ends before the match is over, you lose the match** (a valid result, success 0), also if you never sent `game start`.

## Write a program
You may write a program that observes, measures in the images, computes your next action and sends it, without a
new model response for each action. You stay in the loop: watch its log, and stop, fix and restart it whenever
needed. Only you send `game start` and `game ready`.

- Use only the camera images, the service's replies and this document; no simulator internals or hidden state.
- One action at a time: an action sent before the previous one has returned is refused (HTTP 429).
- Your container: Python 3.12 with numpy, SciPy and Pillow; no internet during the match. Keep your scripts, logs
  and notes in `/app/output/`.

## Interface
Use the `game` command, or the same calls as HTTP with JSON at `http://sim:8000/<SEAT>/` (your seat is `$SEAT`):

| `game` command | HTTP | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `game spec` | `GET /spec` | the actions (types, fields, ranges), the cameras with their intrinsics, the rule constants |
| `game status` | `GET /status` | the current state, no image |
| `game start` | `POST /start {}` | you are ready; the match begins when every seat has started |
| `game wait DT` | `POST /wait {"dt": DT}` | let DT game seconds pass (0 < DT <= 1) |
| `game observe` | `POST /observe {}` | the state and the camera images (one PNG of tiles: `observation.tiles`) |
| `game act JSON` | `POST /act JSON` | one action |
| `game guard ` | `POST /act {"type":"guard", ...}` | one action (`game spec` lists the fields and ranges) |
| `game none ` | `POST /act {"type":"none", ...}` | one action (`game spec` lists the fields and ranges) |
| `game ready "WHY" "PLAN"` | `POST /ready {"why":"...","plan":"..."}` | your review after each of your actions |

Errors: 400 = an invalid action (nothing happens), 409 = not now (not your turn, or a review is due), 429 = one
action in flight, or more than 20 requests per second or 4 open requests from your seat (empty body: retry more slowly).

## Rules
- two identical Franka Panda arms (held to the real robot's joint velocity, acceleration, jerk, torque and torque-rate limits), each on a 0.90 m pedestal on a cart running on a rail (a Festo EGC-TB-185 axis held to 2 m/s, 6 m/s^2 and 150 m/s^3) along a regulation 14 m piste and holding an epee (0.90 m blade, 13.5 cm bell guard), fence one FIE pool bout (5 touches or 3 minutes, no draws; one minute without a touch is unwillingness to fight, FIE t.124) in MuJoCo; blades, guards and bodies collide physically and the electric apparatus is modelled on the point's force along the blade; format bout: you against a scripted fencer (levels 1-3, `game spec` opponent_level), format duel: two players.
- `bout`: one FIE pool bout (t.38): the first to 5 touches wins; 3 minutes of fencing time (the clock runs only while the world runs); at time the fencer ahead wins; at equal scores one more minute for a deciding touch with priority drawn by lot before it (seeded), the priority holder winning if still equal; a double touch counts for both except at 4-4 (not counted); in the extra minute a double leaves the scores equal. Unwillingness to fight (FIE t.124): one minute of fencing time (60 s of the bout clock) without a touch halts the bout; the first time both fencers get a P-red card, a penalty touch each; the second time the fencer with the lower score gets the P-black card and loses the bout (at equal scores: the one who loses a lot, seeded); no card at 4-4 (the minute restarts); the minute restarts after every touch (also a double, an annulled double and a rear-limit touch), not after a corps-a-corps; it does not apply in the extra minute (observation `passivity`: the time without a touch)
- `touch`: only with the point (t.90-t.93): it counts when your point presses on any part of the opponent's robot (cart, pedestal, arm) along the blade with more than 7.35 N for at least 2 ms; on the guard, the blade, the piste or the rail it does not count; the apparatus locks 45 ms after the first touch, a touch by the other fencer before that is a double touch
- `halts`: after every touch; after one minute of fencing time without a touch (unwillingness to fight, t.124); at a corps-a-corps (a cart, pedestal or shoulder touching the other robot; arms and blades touching is close quarters and goes on, t.24-t.25); when a cart goes entirely behind its rear limit, a touch against that fencer (t.34); at the end of time. The world freezes for the review (`game ready WHY PLAN`) after every halt
- `on_guard`: at the start, after a valid touch and before the extra minute the carts are put on the on-guard lines (2 m from the centre line) and the arms in the on-guard pose; after a halt without a touch they stay where they were, each moved back the same distance to 4 m between the carts, a cart in front of its rear limit not put behind it (t.22, t.31)
- `piste`: metres, seconds; your own frame: x along the piste towards the opponent, y to your left, z up, piste surface z = 0; 14 m x 1.5 m, centre line x = 0, on-guard lines x = -2 (yours) and +2, rear limits x = -7 (yours) and +7, run-backs to -9 and +9
- `robot`: a cart (0.5 m long, 0.44 m wide, 0.14 m high) on the rail at y = 0 (|x| <= 7.6; a Festo EGC-TB-185 toothed-belt axis run at 2 m/s, 6 m/s^2 and a jerk of 150 m/s^3 (estimate), motor force at most 2500 N: a time-optimal go-to under these limits, `game spec` robot.rail), a 0.90 m pedestal, the arm's base at 0.90 m and the shoulder at 1.233 m; a Franka Emika Panda arm held to the manufacturer's joint limits (Franka 'Control Interface Specification and Robot Limits', FER; `game spec` robot.arm_limits): velocity 2.175 rad/s joints 1-4, 2.61 rad/s 5-7; acceleration 15, 7.5, 10, 12.5, 15, 20, 20 rad/s^2; jerk 7500, 3750, 5000, 6250, 7500, 10000, 10000 rad/s^3; torque 87 N m joints 1-4, 12 N m 5-7; torque rate 1000 N m/s; planned joint moves are time-optimal S-curves at 95 % of the velocity, acceleration and jerk limits (and of the jerk the torque-rate limit allows at the pose); the robot's 1 kHz servo never commands more than the limits (it smooths any reference to them) and its motor torques change by at most 1 N m per ms; a joint pushed more than 0.02 rad off its setpoint (a hit, a bind) makes the setpoint follow the arm; the epee is held at the flange: grip 0.10 m, bell guard 13.5 cm, blade 0.90 m, the point 1.04 m in front of the grip; on guard the point is at (1.40, -0.05, 1.10) in the cart frame pointing along (1, 0, -0.05); the point reaches about 1.75 m in front of the cart's centre; contacts (blades, guards, arms, bodies) are simulated (MuJoCo, 1 ms steps)
- `actions_high`: act {t, tip [u, v, z], dir [du, dv, dz], rail [x, vmax] (optional)}: the point at (u, v, z) in your cart frame (u forward from the cart's centre, v left, z up from the piste; 0 <= u <= 2, |v| <= 0.8, 0.1 <= z <= 2) with the blade along dir, T s after the command takes effect (0 <= T <= 3) or as soon as the joint limits allow (reply: arrive_s, limited_by_joints; ik_residual > 0.002 = out of reach, the arm goes to the nearest pose it can); move {rail [x] or [x, vmax]}: the rail goal only (|x| <= 7.6, 0.05 <= vmax <= 2 m/s); guard: the arm back on guard; none: the arm stops where it is. An act takes effect at the first 10 ms control step after its IK is ready, the others at the next step; a new arm command replaces the one under way, the cart keeps going to its rail goal
- `actions_low`: joints {q (7 arm joint goals, rad), t, rail_x, rail_vmax (optional)}: a time-optimal jerk-limited joint-space move under the arm's limits (no IK: the kinematic chain is in `game spec` kinematics); move {x, vmax}: the rail goal; hold: the arm stops; traj {q: rows [x, q1..q7]}: 100 Hz joint position targets (one row per 10 ms step; the arm within the velocity limits and the acceleration limits, second differences / (10 ms)^2, the servo smoothing them to the jerk limits; the rail column within the rail's 2 m/s, 6 m/s^2 and 150 m/s^3, first, second and third differences, joined to the rail's last three targets; refused otherwise, and first rows that do not join the current targets within the limits are rejected at the effect; after the last row the rail brakes to rest at it within its limits). Every command takes effect at the next control step
- `observation`: a PNG of 2 rows (side camera beside the piste, top camera above it; poses and intrinsics in `game spec` cameras) x 4 columns (camera frames 20 ms apart, oldest left) of 800 x 360 tiles: your robot red, the opponent blue, the points yellow; no opponent coordinates. The state: score, fencing time, the lamps during the phrase, the last halt, your robot (cart_x, cart_v, the arm joints q, point, guard and blade_dir in your frame, rail goal, whether the arm is still moving) and your command in force
- `scripted_opponent`: format bout: the computer fencer has the same robot and limits; it sees your robot with a reaction delay (level 1: 0.16 s, 2: 0.10 s, 3: 0.06 s) and plays one of its level's actions per phrase (level 1: attacks, attacks on preparation, distance play, feints; level 2 adds beats, parries, stop-hits, running attacks; level 3 beats, counter-beats, derobements, parries, retreats, low and running attacks, preferring what has scored); a phrase without a halt for 5 s makes it attack on the blade
- Winner: the first to 5 touches wins (FIE t.38); a second minute without a touch (unwillingness to fight, FIE t.124) loses the bout for the fencer with the lower score, at equal scores for the one who loses a lot (seeded); at the end of the 3 minutes the fencer ahead wins; at equal scores one more minute is fenced and the first touch decides; if the scores are still equal after it, the fencer with priority, drawn by lot (seeded) before the extra minute, wins (FIE t.38.2.b). There are no draws.
- Deviation D1 (rulebook t.28, t.33, t.35): footwork is a cart on a rail along the piste's centre line: no lateral boundaries and no passing
- Deviation D2 (rulebook t.91, m.19, Material Rules Annexe B): the robot's whole structure (cart, pedestal, arm) is the target; the apparatus measures the force on the point along the blade (> 7.35 N for >= 2 ms, three consecutive 1 ms samples; lockout 45 ms, inside the 40-50 ms tolerance)
- Deviation D3 (rulebook t.24, t.25): corps-a-corps needs a trunk (cart, pedestal, shoulder) in contact with the other robot; arm-on-arm and blade contact is fencing at close quarters and goes on
- Deviation D4 (rulebook t.31, t.32): after a corps-a-corps both fencers move back equally (t.31 instead of t.32)
- Deviation D7 (rulebook -): the arms are Franka Panda arms held to the manufacturer's joint limits (velocity 2.175 / 2.61 rad/s, acceleration 7.5-20 rad/s^2, jerk 3750-10000 rad/s^3, torque 87 / 12 N m, torque rate 1000 N m/s; Franka 'Control Interface Specification and Robot Limits', FER): a full extension from on guard takes 0.55-0.75 s, slower against the footwork than a fencer's arm (fencing-2 used 1.5 x the velocity and acceleration limits: 0.50-0.58 s)
- Deviation D8 (rulebook -): the footwork rail is a Festo EGC-TB-185 toothed-belt axis (catalogue: 5 m/s, 50 m/s^2, feed force 2500 N; Festo operating instructions 8162896, 2023-05) run inside that envelope: 2 m/s, 6 m/s^2, a jerk limit of 150 m/s^3 (an estimate: Festo publishes no jerk limit; the B9 feasibility study's value) and a motor force of at most 2500 N (fencing-4; up to fencing-3 the rail was no real product: 2 m/s, 6 m/s^2, 3000 N, no jerk limit). A 4 m advance at full speed takes about 2.6 s
- Deviation D9 (rulebook t.124, t.170 (0.5)): unwillingness to fight (FIE Technical Rules, August 2026, t.124: 'There is unwillingness to fight when there is one minute of fencing without a hit'; the FIE applies its sanctions to direct-elimination bouts (t.124.1) and team matches (t.124.2), not to pool bouts) applies to our one pool bout, with the direct-elimination sanctions: one minute of fencing time, measured on the bout clock (`fencing_time_s`, effective fencing time as in t.37: 60 s = 6000 control steps of 10 ms; the wall clock takes slowdown x 60 s), without a hit -> 'Halt!'; the first time a P-red card to both fencers, a penalty hit each, both put on guard on the on-guard lines (t.124.1.a, t.22.6); the second time the P-black card to the fencer with the lower score, who loses the bout, at equal scores to the fencer who loses a seeded lot (t.124.1.b.i: lots for fencers not in the FIE ranking, as all of ours); no P-card at 4-4, the pool's 14-14 (t.124.3.a): the halt is called and the minute restarts; the minute restarts after each hit, double, annulled double, rear-limit hit (t.34) and penalty hit (t.124.3.d), not after a corps-a-corps; t.124 does not apply in the extra minute (t.124.3.f). fencing-5; up to fencing-4 a bout could be run out without a hit to the 3 minutes and the extra minute's lot

## Geometry and physics
Everything you need is in `game spec`: the world frame, the release point, the cameras (pose, field of view, size,
`focal_px`, `principal_point_px`; pinhole: u = cx + f * x_right / depth, v = cy - f * y_up / depth) and the
execution scatter. The physics engine is mujoco.
